title: 米LCCスピリットが事業停止へ準備　政府との資金支援交渉が決裂、資金繰りに行き詰まり
extracted_text: 米紙ウォールストリート・ジャーナル（WSJ）は1日、経営破綻した米格安航空会社（LCC）大手のスピリット航空が事業停止に向けた準備に入ったと報じた。米政府による約5億ドル（約780億円）の資金支援を巡る交渉が決裂し、資金繰りが行き詰まりつつあるためとしている。 WSJによると、スピリットはトランプ米政権と、政府が最大9割の株式を取得できる新株予約権を受け取る見返りに資金を注入する案を協議していた。ただ政権内部で支援の是非を巡る対立があったほか、一部の債権者も反対し、合意に至らなかったという。事業停止の時期は明らかになっていない。 トランプ大統領は1日、ホワイトハウスで記者団に「雇用を守りたい」と述べ、救済に改めて意欲を示した。スピリットに対して最終提案をしたと明らかにし、近く内容を発表すると強調した。
translated_text: The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported on the 1st that Spirit Airlines, a major U.S. low-cost carrier (LCC) that has filed for bankruptcy, has begun preparations to halt operations. This is because negotiations for about $5 billion (approximately 780 billion yen) in financial support from the U.S. government have broken down, and cash flow has become increasingly tight. According to WSJ, Spirit had been discussing a proposal with the Trump administration to inject funds in exchange for new share subscription rights that would allow the government to acquire up to 90% of the stock. However, there were divisions within the administration over whether to provide support, and some creditors also opposed it, leading to no agreement. The timing of the potential shutdown has not been determined. President Trump said at the White House on the 1st that he wants to protect jobs, reiterating his determination to pursue a rescue. He revealed that he made a final proposal to Spirit and emphasized that he would announce the details soon.
title_en: U.S. LCC Spirit Prepares for Shutdown as Government Funding Negotiations Break Down, Cash Flow Stalled
